title.narrative: Micronesia: Tourism Support for Biodiversity Conservation

description.narrative: Ecosystems and livelihoods in Yap and Kosrae states of FSM supported by the tourism sector through creation of an enabling and conducive environment enhanced by conservation and NbS policies
Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

The project is designed to bring about numerous economic and social benefits. It involves the active participation of various stakeholders, including national and state administrations, private operators, civil society, and local communities, which encompass both land and marine spaces as well as private property owners. At the national level, key stakeholders will include the executing agencies, the Office of Statistics, which will supply raw data for various studies and analyses, including NCA, and the Ministry of Finance, which will provide financial data and offer oversight and guidance on the financial aspects related to the NCA approach and the SEEA.A key feature of the project is the allocation of specific budget lines aimed at financially supporting local communities and private operators. This funding will be directed towards developing and enhancing small-scale responsible eco-tourism initiatives, which are anticipated to generate tangible socio-economic benefits at the local level.Additionally, the project has incorporated a gender dimension into its design to ensure the effective participation of women and specific groups in its implementation. This approach aims to foster inclusivity and equity within the project's framework.The expected social benefits of the project are manifold. Among these are improved income levels for local communities, facilitated by a strengthened value chain in tourism. Nature-based tourism, in particular, is projected to create both direct and indirect economic benefits for communities, including those members who may not engage directly with tourists.By aligning tourism development with broader conservation goals, the project aims to ensure that local communities reap the benefits of tourism in a manner that supports a sustainable local economy. Furthermore, the project will promote collective engagement and learning. This component seeks to ensure that the benefits of the project extend beyond the immediate term, contributing to long-term sustainable development at the local level and enhancing environmental conservation efforts within the Federated States of Micronesia (FSM).
